input:
Snapdragon X2 Elite ('Glymur') BSP on Linux 6.18 shows the thermal zone temperatures reading ~15-20°C higher than an IR-camera measurement of the die surface:

  thermal_zone7 temp: 97000 (i.e. 97°C)   # IR camera: 79°C
  thermal_zone9 temp: 102000 (i.e. 102°C)  # IR camera: 82°C

This aggressive TSENS bias is causing the governor to clamp CPU freq too early. The qcom-tsens driver on 6.18 added Glymur support. What manufacturing-time calibration mechanism is used, and why does the bootloader's failure to propagate calibration data make the TSENS readings raw ADC counts instead of °C? What device-tree property is involved?
